claims.text: Preheating the build platform during additive manufacturing of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi reduces thermal gradients.
Build-platform preheating minimizes residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Build-platform preheating reduces defect formation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Build-platform preheating reduces compositional segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
AlCrFeNiSi processed with an ambient-temperature substrate conventionally exhibits segregation during cooling.
AlCrFeNiSi processed with an ambient-temperature substrate conventionally exhibits residual-stress-induced defects.
A substrate temperature of 300–500 °C is an applicable preheating range for laser-based additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating controls the cooling rate during additive manufacturing.
A moderated solidification thermal gradient permits more gradual phase formation and diffusion.
More gradual phase formation and diffusion reduce microsegregation and stress accumulation.
Preheating decreases the temperature differential between the melt pool and the substrate.
A smaller melt-pool-to-substrate temperature differential produces a slower cooling rate.
Slower cooling promotes more uniform solidification and thereby minimizes compositional segregation.
Slower cooling decreases the accumulation of residual thermal stress and consequently reduces defect formation.
Relative to room-temperature-substrate processing, preheated AlCrFeNiSi builds will have lower residual stress.
Relative to room-temperature-substrate processing, preheated AlCrFeNiSi builds will have less grain-boundary segregation and fewer processing defects.
Reduced residual stress, segregation, and defect density will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed effect is expected to hold for laser-based additive manufacturing of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi within the 300–500 °C preheat range.
Substrate preheating has reduced thermal gradients in similar alloy systems.
